title: Comparative Impact of ChatGPT and Conventional Search Tools on Clinical Reasoning Performance: A Randomized Crossover Study in Preclinical Medical Students
venue: Advances in Medical Education and Practice
extended_summary:
This paper addresses whether generative AI tools, specifically ChatGPT, improve clinical reasoning performance among medical students compared with conventional information-search strategies such as Google or PubMed. The authors frame the problem around the growing use of large language models in medical education, noting both their potential to organize information efficiently and their risks, including hallucinated or inaccurate outputs and overreliance by learners.

The study used a randomized crossover design during a musculoskeletal system course. Forty-six second-year medical students at Kasetsart University completed a baseline clinical reasoning pre-test, then worked through standardized clinical cases using either ChatGPT or conventional search tools. After a post-test, a 60-minute washout period, and crossover to the alternate modality, students completed a second post-test. Clinical reasoning was assessed with an eight-point rubric covering problem representation, differential diagnosis, investigations, and initial management; students also provided self-perceived learning, confidence, and qualitative feedback.

Mean clinical reasoning scores improved from 3.96 at baseline to 4.96 after the first intervention and 5.70 after crossover, with statistically significant gains across all paired comparisons and a large cumulative effect size. The study did not find evidence that gains were attributable to only one tool: ChatGPT helped students rapidly organize differential diagnoses and management plans, while conventional search encouraged comparison across sources and deliberate synthesis.

The authors conclude that both AI-assisted and conventional search strategies can support short-term clinical reasoning when embedded in structured active-learning activities. They recommend balanced integration of large language models alongside traditional search methods, with faculty oversight and explicit emphasis on verifying AI-generated information against reliable sources.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: ChatGPT is an OpenAI large language model chatbot that generates conversational, context-sensitive responses and can synthesize information for learning support.
identified_tools.use_case: Second-year medical students used ChatGPT with self-directed prompting during 20-minute structured case-based learning activities to analyze standardized musculoskeletal clinical cases, generate differential diagnoses, and consider investigations and management plans; performance was compared in a crossover design against conventional search tools.

findings.finding_summary: In a randomized crossover study of 46 second-year medical students, mean clinical reasoning scores increased from 3.96 ± 1.65 at pre-test to 4.96 ± 1.71 after the first intervention and 5.70 ± 1.50 after crossover. Paired comparisons were statistically significant for pre-test to post-test 1 (t(45)=-3.79, p<0.05), post-test 1 to post-test 2 (t(45)=-2.96, p<0.05), and pre-test to post-test 2 (t(45)=-6.57, p<0.05), with a large cumulative effect size of Cohen’s d=0.97. The authors state that improvements occurred across both ChatGPT and conventional search modalities, without evidence that gains were attributable to a single approach.
findings.measure: Clinical reasoning performance measured using an eight-point rubric-based scale assessing problem representation, differential diagnoses, investigations, and initial management
findings.effect_size: Cohen’s d=0.56 for pre-test to post-test 1; Cohen’s d=0.44 for post-test 1 to post-test 2; Cohen’s d=0.97 for pre-test to post-test 2

findings.finding_summary: Students reported that ChatGPT facilitated rapid organization of differential diagnoses and management plans during structured clinical case analysis. Qualitative feedback also emphasized the importance of verifying AI outputs against reliable references.
findings.measure: Self-perceived learning, confidence, and qualitative feedback from structured evaluation forms

quality_tier_rationale: This was a randomized crossover study with all 46 participants completing both intervention phases and within-subject comparisons reported. Quality is downgraded from blue because it was single-institution, short-term, had potential residual period/carryover effects, and did not report modality-specific effects isolating ChatGPT from conventional search.
impact_tier_rationale: The study reports statistically significant improvements in clinical reasoning scores with moderate-to-large effect sizes, including a large cumulative effect from pre-test to post-test 2 (Cohen’s d=0.97). However, gains were observed across both ChatGPT and conventional search modalities and were not attributable to ChatGPT alone.
